channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) developed a GRADE-based clinical practice guideline for rehabilitating athletes with hamstring strain injury, synthesizing evidence from randomized clinical trials.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Photobiomodulation therapy has a negligible effect as an adjunct to motor control exercise in people with chronic non-specific low back pain: a randomised trial.
item.description: A randomized trial (n=148) found that adding photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) to motor control exercise (MCE) for chronic non-specific low back pain had a negligible effect on pain intensity (MD -0.4 points, 95% CI -1.2 to 0.4) and disability (MD -0.7 points, 95% CI -2.4 to 0.9) at 6 weeks and over 12 months, compared with sham PBMT plus MCE.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: A case series of 100 patients after QT-ACLR showed that early 3-month isometric quadriceps LSI strongly predicted 2-year IKDC scores (β = 3.9; Adj R² = 0.36; P < .03), with patients achieving PASS typically reaching a 60%-70% LSI by 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post burn Cubital Tunnel Syndrome Electrophysiological and Functional Responses to High intensity Laser Therapy versus Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=75) on post-burn cubital tunnel syndrome found that high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) combined with ulnar nerve gliding exercises produced significantly greater improvements in nerve conduction velocity, CMAP amplitudes, and DASH scores compared to extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) or exercises alone, with benefits maintained at 12-week follow-up (all P < .001).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: A theoretical framework proposes conceptualizing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process (HODA-A), rather than isolated manual techniques, and applies COSMIN principles for its evaluation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 30 chronic post-stroke hemiplegia patients found that thoracic kinesiology taping combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1, PEF, all p < 0.001) and inspiratory muscle strength (MIP, p < 0.001) compared to sham taping.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial of 81 cervicogenic headache patients found that both kinesio taping and myofascial release, combined with home exercise, effectively reduced pain and improved quality of life, with MFR showing more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life at one-month follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review found no clear association between reduced spinal ROM and outcomes for various spinal pain conditions, with consistently very low certainty of evidence and high risk of bias across studies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of physiotherapy in reducing pain in subjects with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review with network meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis (25 RCTs, n=1,540) found manual therapy (MT) and therapeutic exercise (TE) effective for reducing pain in temporomandibular disorders (TMDs). Multimodal treatments were most effective, with the combination of dry needling and manual therapy appearing to be the best approach.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effectiveness of conservative interventions on pain and disability in degenerative cervical spine disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (2,378 participants) found that conservative interventions significantly reduced pain (SMD = −0.67) and disability (SMD = −0.60) in degenerative cervical spine disease. Acupuncture and exercise-based interventions showed significant benefits, while manual therapy did not show a significant pooled benefit. Evidence certainty was low.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 studies (1,177 participants) found that chronic physical exercise training improved the metabolic cost of walking (Cw) in healthy individuals (g=0.49), but not significantly in stroke patients (g=0.24, p=0.065). Higher BMI was associated with smaller intervention effects on Cw (β=-0.20). Population type moderated the effects of training on Cw (p=0.043).
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 97 adolescent patients found that an ACL-RSI score ≥59.2 was associated with a 3.56 odds ratio (95% CI, 1.10-11.51; P = .033) for successful return to sport after patellar stabilization surgery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A multicenter randomized controlled trial found that a smartphone-based digital therapeutic combining personalized exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy significantly reduced pain and improved function, quality of life, and psychological well-being in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Six-month supervised telerehabilitation combining pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release in adults with fibromyalgia: a randomized controlled trial | Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine
item.description: A 6-month supervised telerehabilitation program combining Pilates-based exercise and self-myofascial release significantly improved fibromyalgia impact, sleep quality, and depressive symptoms compared to usual care in this RCT.
item.author: J Rehabil Med

item.title: Association of dysphagia with physical performance and fall risk in frail older adults
item.description: This study found dysphagia in frail older adults is linked to decreased physical performance (SPPB) and increased fall risk, highlighting the need for routine swallowing assessments in geriatric care.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: From information to action; co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain: Focus group insights.
item.description: Focus group discussions with 15 adolescents (15-19 years old) with low back pain revealed four key themes for co-designing pain neuroscience education (PNE): need for recognition ("This is about me"), practical tools ("What can I do myself?"), engaging format ("Otherwise I will stop reading"), and easy navigation ("It must be easy to find").
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Early Changes in Post-Stroke Quality of Life and Associated Factors: A Prospective Study.
item.description: A prospective study of 111 stroke patients found that physical HRQoL improved progressively over 3 months, while mental HRQoL improved only in the first month. Functional ambulation was associated with physical HRQoL change (β = 0.483, p < 0.001), and depressive symptom severity with mental HRQoL change (β = -0.692, p < 0.001).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Barriers and facilitators of decision-making in home-based rehabilitation exercise among older adults following total knee arthroplasty: A qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study with 21 older adults after total knee arthroplasty identified three themes regarding home-based rehabilitation decision-making: intuitive avoidance responses (pain-triggered avoidance, fear), external support constraints (inadequate guidance, limited family support), and rational adherence (perceived threat of poor prognosis, willpower).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Recent highlights in pulmonary rehabilitation research.
item.description: This narrative review highlighted five key themes in pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) research from January 2021 to May 2026: improving access, uptake, and completion; extending PR beyond stable COPD to other chronic respiratory diseases; developing alternative PR models; maintaining benefits post-PR; and economic analyses of PR.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adherence to home-based exercise therapy in adults with non-specific chronic low back pain: a cross-sectional study of 491 participants of the ComPaRE cLBP e-cohort (ADHERE II).
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 491 adults with non-specific chronic low back pain found that adherence to home-based exercise therapy was 45%, with no significant influence of supervision. Higher baseline physical activity, lower pain intensity, and lower treatment burden were associated with higher adherence.
item.author: PubMed
